en: Itivuttaka 85:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on Contemplating the Unattractive.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Monks, dwell contemplating the unattractive in the body."
And let mindfulness of breathing be well-established within you, facing inward;
dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned phenomena.
For those, monks, who dwell contemplating foulness in the body, that underlying tendency toward lust for the element of beauty is abandoned.

"Through the well-established mindfulness of breathing directed inwardly toward the face, those external tendencies of thought that are a source of corruption and belong to the side of affliction do not arise.
For those who dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned phenomena, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"Contemplating the foulness in the body,
mindful of the breath;"
Seeing the stilling of all formations, ever ardent—
he indeed is the bhikkhu who sees rightly.
Since he is liberated therein,
having reached the culmination of direct knowledge and being at peace—
he is indeed the sage who has transcended all bonds.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The sixth [discourse].
